warmup.text: Chapter 22 takes Naomi somewhere nobody would think to look. Part of it explains how some Choctaw women cared for people who had died. Read it calmly. Today you will reread one sentence and notice how it is built.

words.text: Put the light words to work today. Then try book words you have never studied. Break each one into its parts, and work out the meaning before anyone tells you. Then four new lanterns.

reading.text: Read Chapter 22 in your book. Watch who welcomes Naomi, and why their wagon is the safest place for her. Then reread the thunderbolt sentence in the Read Like a Writer box, and finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 22. Then revise your paragraph with the checklist. Check every he, she and they. Improve one transition. Cut words you do not need. Show one sentence before and after.

hook.q: Soldiers are hunting for a girl. Where would you hide her?

options.reply: The woods are a good guess, but soldiers search there first. The women in Chapter 22 have a stranger idea:
Hiding in plain sight is clever. The women in Chapter 22 go even further:
A good hiding place, if nobody looks. The women in Chapter 22 pick a place soldiers will not want to look:

reveal.line: This is the safest place for you now.
reveal.cite: a woman in the wagon, Chapter 22
reveal.then: As you read Chapter 22, find out where Naomi hides, and why the soldiers will not want to look there.

game.title: Light the Lanterns
game.sub: This week's word game · 4 words today
game.look: Each lantern on the branch waits for one word. Read the meaning, then tap the word parts in order to build the word. When the word is whole, its lantern lights up.

art.title: Roses in a Bowl
art.alt: A painting of pink, white, red and yellow roses in a dark bowl on a brown table.
art.look: Henri Fantin-Latour painted these roses in France in 1883. The book does not show the wagon, but it tells you how it smells: Naomi climbs into a wagon sweetened by the smell of dried roses.

virtue.name: perseverance
virtue.title: The perseverance meter
virtue.intro: Think about one moment from Chapter 22.
virtue.moment: Naomi lies in a secret space at the bottom of a trunk, under a blanket in the dark. The air is stuffy, and she can hear the wagon rattle, but she stays still and waits.
virtue.ask: How much perseverance did Naomi show? Slide to show.
virtue.take: Mason's take: a lot. She was scared, and she stayed. Sometimes perseverance means holding still and waiting.
